title: History of two mass loss processes in VY CMa. Fast outflows carving older ejecta
question: What are the spatio-kinematical characteristics and physical origins of the mass loss ejections in the red supergiant VY CMa?

data.angular_resolution: ~0.025 arcsec (25-35 mas; synthetic beam 29 x 25 mas)
data.sensitivity: ~0.15 mJy Beam^-1 per channel; 0.028-0.052 mJy Beam^-1 in continuum

what.value: Distance to VY CMa of 1.2 kpc

evidence.quote: On the other hand, VY CMa, a RSG located at a distance of 1.2 kpc (cite: Zhang12), presents a massive ejecta very rich in molecular species with an oxygen-rich chemistry (cite: Zyuris07; Tenenbaum10) that can be studied in detail.

what.value: Inclination of blob D (~15 deg) used as upper limit for inclination of outflow C

evidence.quote: We thus can assume that the inclination of *C* is equal to or lower than that of blob *D*, which was $\sim 15^\circ$ (cite: Kaminski19).

what.value: Dust mass of clump C and gas-to-dust ratio of 200 giving total mass of 0.05 M_sun

evidence.quote: We adopt the higher value for the dust mass of *C* derived by (cite: ogorman15) with a gas-to-dust ratio of 200. The total mass of the outflow is therefore 0.05$M_{\odot}$.

what.value: Size of cold spots in RSGs of 2.8 x 10^23 cm^2

evidence.quote: The size of the cold spots in the RSGs has been found (cite: kunstler15) to reach sizes of $2.8 \times10^{23}$ cm$^2$, and the time estimated for the formation of the *C*-outflow is $\sim$50 years.

what.value: Rotation velocity of RSGs (~1 km s^-1)

evidence.quote: The rotation velocity of RSGs is estimated to be $\sim$1km s$^{-1}$ (cite: Zhang12), while for some objects such as Betelgeuse values as high as 15km s$^{-1}$ have been derived (cite: Wheeler17).

what.value: Stellar radius of VY CMa of R_* = 9.9 x 10^13 cm

evidence.quote: With a stellar radius of VY CMa of $R_{\star} = 9.9 \times 10^{13}$cm (cite: Wittkowski12) the effect of the rotation should be seen in a collimated outflow with the formation times derived.

recipe.goal: Identify molecular transitions in the spectral windows
recipe.method: Line identification across the four spectral windows using the MADEX spectroscopic catalog

recipe.goal: Extract position-velocity diagrams and fit expansion velocity law of localized outflows
recipe.method: Construct position-velocity (PV) diagrams of NaCl v=0,1 and H2S emission along the main axes connecting VY to structures A and C, and fit a linear (Hubble-like) expansion velocity law V_exp proportional to r
key_parameters: Inclination of outflow C assumed <= 15 deg
assumptions: Hubble-like linear velocity field v proportional to r

recipe.goal: Reconstruct 3D spatial structure of the fast outflows and determine stellar position and V_LSR
recipe.method: Convert spectral cubes (R.A., Dec., velocity) of H2S, NaCl, and o-H2O into 3D spatial coordinates by cropping below 3 sigma and transforming velocity into line-of-sight distance using the fitted Hubble-like velocity law
assumptions: Same Hubble-like velocity field applies to all fast outflows and inner o-H2O outflows

recipe.goal: Compare fast outflows with cavities in the extended regular ejecta
recipe.method: Overplot velocity-shifted H2S emission onto SO channel maps to test spatial correspondence between fast jets and SO shell cavities

recipe.goal: Estimate linear momentum and required magnetic field for CME-like ejection of clump C
recipe.method: Calculate linear momentum of clump C from adopted mass and Hubble velocity law, and use CME momentum transfer rate scaling from Welsch (2018) to derive required surface magnetic field strength
key_parameters: Outflow C total mass = 0.05 M_sun; cold spot area = 2.8 x 10^23 cm^2; formation time = 50 yr
assumptions: Gas-to-dust ratio = 200; constant mass distribution along the ejecta; momentum transfer rate of 1 g cm s^-1 per cm^2 per s for B = 3 G proportional to B_perp

recipe.goal: Model flattened outflows with a rotating stellar spot (Sprinkler model)
recipe.method: Simulate gas ejection from active spots at latitude theta_i and initial rotation angle phi_i on a rotating star, with expansion velocity modulated by a sinusoid over activity duration t_e, and match to 3D H2S structures
key_parameters: Rotation axis angle ~95 deg around R.A. axis; v_rot = 1 km s^-1 (also tested 15 km s^-1); R_* = 9.9 x 10^13 cm; V_16 = 94.4 and 85.9 km s^-1; t_e = 10 yr
assumptions: Distance = 1.2 kpc; stellar radius R_* = 9.9 x 10^13 cm; sinusoidal velocity modulation during spot activity

evidence.quote: Assuming this inclination for the *C* jet, we found we could fit the expansion velocity to $v = 17 \times r/0\mbox{\rlap{.}$''$}1\, \mbox{km~s$^{-1}$}$.

evidence.quote: In addition, the fitting of the outflow connecting $VY$ and $C$ suggests the systemic velocity at $VY$ might not be 22 km s$^{-1}$ as previously thought (cite: Decin16; Richards14), but $V_{LSR}=$12 km s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Alternative LSR velocity suggested by larger northern VY-A jet

evidence.quote: The jet pointing away from us suggests a source velocity similar to that of jet *C*, while the larger jet suggests a LSR velocity of 26 km s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Inclination of northern jet in VY-A

evidence.quote: If we impose the same velocity field, the inclination for the northern jet is 4.5$^\circ$ and that of the rear jet is -30$^\circ$.

answer_key.quantity: Inclination of rear jet in VY-A

evidence.quote: If we impose the same velocity field, the inclination for the northern jet is 4.5$^\circ$ and that of the rear jet is -30$^\circ$.

answer_key.quantity: Angular extent of VY-C and VY-A outflows

evidence.quote: The extent of the $VY$–$C$ and $VY$–$A$ outflows is similar, around $\sim 0\mbox{\rlap{.}$''$}7-0\mbox{\rlap{.}$''$}8$, which corresponds to $1.3-1.5 \times 10^{16}$cm, and reaches a velocity of $\sim 120-140\mbox{km~s$^{-1}$}$ at the tip of these outflows.

answer_key.quantity: Maximum velocity at tip of VY-C and VY-A outflows

answer_key.quantity: Formation timescale of VY-C and VY-A outflows

evidence.quote: The formation of these structures took $\sim 50-60$ years, confirming the timescales suggested above (cite: ogorman15).

answer_key.quantity: Number of fast outflows identified in 3D H2S reconstruction

evidence.quote: Thanks to the 3D reconstruction, at least six outflows can be identified in the structure obtained, especially from the H$_2$S maps (see red arrows in Fig. 4).

answer_key.quantity: Number of inner outflows identified in o-H2O maser emission

evidence.quote: At least two inner outflows have been identified from the o-H$_2$O $5_{5,0}-6_{4,3}$ $v_2=1$ emission.

answer_key.quantity: Width-to-height ratio of flattened fast outflows

evidence.quote: The ratio of width to height is $\sim\,6$.

answer_key.quantity: Total linear momentum of outflow C

evidence.quote: The total momentum driven by this ejection assuming the Hubble velocity field deduced above and a constant mass distribution along the ejecta is $P = 9.30 \times 10^{38}$ g cm s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Magnetic field strength needed to drive outflow C momentum

evidence.quote: The magnetic field needed to provide the amount of momentum derived above is $\sim$5kG.

answer_key.quantity: Rotation axis angle around R.A. axis in Sprinkler model

evidence.quote: In this sense, we have found a particular angle ($\sim$95$^\circ$) around the R.A. axis, which seems to be compatible with this scenario.

answer_key.quantity: Sprinkler model Hubble velocity at 10^16 cm (V_16) for outflows 1 and 2
Sprinkler model Hubble velocity at 10^16 cm (V_16) for outflows 3, 4, and 5
Ejection activity duration (t_e) for V_rot = 1 km s^-1
Ejection activity duration (t_e) for V_rot = 15 km s^-1

evidence.quote: Therefore, for a $V_{rot}=15\mbox{km~s$^{-1}$}$ the value of $t_e$ would be eight months.

answer_key.quantity: Time interval between ejections for V_rot = 1 km s^-1

evidence.quote: For a rotation velocity of 1km s$^{-1}$ we found that the time between the ejections was in the range $\sim$1 – 6 years, being the time between the first and the last ejection $\sim$11 years.

answer_key.quantity: Time interval between ejections for V_rot = 15 km s^-1

evidence.quote: For a $v_{rot}$ of 15km s$^{-1}$ the range would be $\sim$1 – 5 months and $\sim$9 months between the first and last ejection.
